quests.instruction: Putting books back on a shelf is tidying. Which of these is cleaning?
options: Hanging a jacket on a hook 🧥
quests.hint: Tidying puts things in their place. Cleaning removes dirt.
quests.explanation: Tidying means putting things where they belong. Cleaning removes dust, dirt, and germs. Wiping the shelf takes dirt away.
quests.funFact: A room can be tidy but not clean, or clean but not tidy.

quests.instruction: Why does it help to tidy up before sweeping a floor?
quests.correctAnswer: Toys and shoes block the broom 🧹
options: Toys and shoes block the broom 🧹
Dust cannot land in a tidy room 🌫️
quests.hint: A broom cannot sweep where things are in the way.
quests.explanation: Clutter makes it hard to reach the dust and crumbs underneath. Tidying first clears the way for cleaning.
quests.funFact: Clearing the floor first is why cleaners often start by picking things up.

quests.instruction: A playroom has toys all over the floor and a sticky juice spot. What does it need?
quests.hint: Look at what each problem needs.
quests.explanation: Toys need tidying, and sticky juice needs cleaning, so the room needs both. Doing only one leaves a problem behind.
quests.funFact: Many tidy-up songs for children end with a wipe of the table.

quests.instruction: When sorting a toy box, which pile is for a toy that is broken beyond repair?
quests.hint: Ask whether anyone else could use it.
quests.explanation: A toy that cannot be fixed would not be fun or safe for anyone else, so it goes to the trash. Good toys can be kept or given away.
quests.funFact: Some broken toys can be fixed with a little glue or a new battery.

quests.instruction: While sorting a drawer, Leo finds a pen that does not write, a ruler, and a good pencil. Which goes in the trash?
quests.hint: One of them can no longer do the job it was made for.
quests.explanation: A pen that does not write has stopped doing its job. The ruler and pencil still work and can stay.
quests.funFact: A pen that has run out of ink can sometimes be recycled, depending on where you live.

quests.instruction: Which three things should stay together in the 'art' pile?
quests.hint: Look for things you would use for the same activity.
quests.explanation: Crayons, paper, and glue are all used for making art, so they belong together. The other groups mix unrelated things.
quests.funFact: Art supplies kept in one box are quick to set up and quick to put away.

quests.instruction: Which surfaces in a home get touched the most, and need wiping often?
options: The inside of a closed drawer 🗃️
quests.hint: Ask yourself what many hands touch each day.
quests.explanation: Handles and switches pick up germs from everyone who uses them. Hidden spots hardly get touched.
quests.funFact: Touched surfaces get wiped more often in homes where someone is sick.

quests.instruction: A damp cloth works better than a dry one on sticky fingerprints. Why?
options: A dry cloth makes it stickier 🧻
quests.hint: Water helps sticky things let go.
quests.explanation: A damp cloth loosens sticky patches so they wipe away. A dry cloth just drags them around.
quests.funFact: A little soap on the cloth helps with greasy marks too.

quests.instruction: A glass leaves water on a shiny wooden table. What should you do?
quests.hint: Water left on wood can leave a mark.
quests.explanation: Wiping water up right away protects wood from marks and swelling. Leaving it or covering it can make a stain.
quests.funFact: Coasters stop water rings from forming in the first place.

quests.instruction: Why are white shirts usually washed apart from a new bright red towel?
options: Towels make shirts far too heavy ⚖️
quests.hint: New colors can bleed in water.
quests.explanation: New, bright cloth can release dye in the wash and stain light clothes. Sorting by color prevents it.
quests.funFact: Laundry is often sorted into lights, darks, and colors.

quests.instruction: What do the symbols on a clothing label tell you?
quests.correctAnswer: How to wash and dry it 📋
options: How to wash and dry it 📋
quests.hint: The label has instructions for caring for the cloth.
quests.explanation: Care labels show how hot the water can be and how to dry the item. Following them keeps clothes from shrinking or fading.
quests.funFact: A hand-in-a-tub symbol often means to wash by hand.

quests.instruction: Clothes come out of the wash still damp. What is the right next step?
options: Put them in a drawer damp 🗄️
quests.hint: Damp clothes put away stay damp and smell.
quests.explanation: Clothes should be completely dry before they are folded or stored. Damp cloth can grow mildew and smell musty.
quests.funFact: Hanging clothes in a breezy spot helps them dry faster.

quests.instruction: Where recycling is collected, which of these usually goes in the recycling bin?
quests.hint: Recycling is for clean materials that can be made into something new.
quests.explanation: Clean plastic bottles can be turned into new items. Used tissues and food scraps are not recyclable and go elsewhere.
quests.funFact: Some plastic bottles are made into fleece clothing, carpets, or new bottles.

quests.instruction: Why do recycling rules differ from town to town?
quests.correctAnswer: Each place has its own rules 🏘️
options: Bins get tired of old things 🗑️
Each place has its own rules 🏘️
quests.hint: Different places use different machines and companies.
quests.explanation: Each town or city decides what its recycling plant can handle. A local website or a grown-up can tell you what is accepted.
quests.funFact: A symbol with arrows on a package does not always mean it can be recycled where you live.

quests.instruction: Before putting a jar in the recycling, what should you do?
options: Crush it flat with your foot 🦶
quests.hint: Leftover food can spoil the whole batch.
quests.explanation: A quick rinse removes food that could spoil other recycling. Never crush glass with your foot, since it could break and cut you.
quests.funFact: A jar can be reused for storing things, instead of being recycled.

quests.instruction: A grown-up is about to use the vacuum cleaner. What should a child do first?
quests.correctAnswer: Pick up small toys and socks 🧦
options: Cover the vacuum with a towel 🧺
Pick up small toys and socks 🧦
quests.hint: The vacuum works best on a clear floor.
quests.explanation: Small things can get stuck in a vacuum or block it, so picking them up helps. The grown-up then runs the vacuum.
quests.funFact: Vacuums often have a loud motor, so some children prefer to play in another room.

quests.instruction: Which tool picks up crumbs from a carpet, used by a grown-up?
quests.hint: A carpet needs suction, not water.
quests.explanation: A vacuum sucks dust and crumbs out of carpet fibers. A wet mop would soak the carpet, and a dust cloth only reaches the top.
quests.funFact: Some vacuums have a brush that spins to loosen dirt from the carpet.

quests.instruction: A clean sweater fell on the floor. What is the best thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Shake it out and check it 🧥
options: Put it back in the drawer 🗄️
Shake it out and check it 🧥
quests.hint: The floor may have left dust or dirt behind.
quests.explanation: Shaking it out and looking tells you whether it is still clean. Putting it back may spread dirt, and leaving it makes the floor messy.
quests.funFact: Many people keep a hamper nearby so doubtful clothes have an easy place to go.

quests.instruction: A family keeps batteries, tape, and string in one drawer. How are the things grouped?
options: By the age of each item 🎂
quests.hint: Look at what the three have in common.
quests.explanation: These are all small helper items for fixing or making things. Grouping by use makes things easy to find.
quests.funFact: A drawer for odds and ends is sometimes called the junk drawer.

quests.instruction: Which container is best for lots of tiny building bricks?
quests.hint: Small pieces roll, spill, and slip away.
quests.explanation: A box with a lid holds many small pieces and keeps them from rolling away. A flat plate or a torn bag lets them escape.
quests.funFact: Shallow trays help sort small pieces by shape or color.

quests.instruction: A shelf is so crowded that nothing can be found. What improves it most?
quests.hint: Where can your eyes and hands find each thing?
quests.explanation: Leaving some space and grouping like things lets you see and reach what you need. Extra rows and curtains hide things more.
quests.funFact: Experts suggest leaving about a third of a shelf empty so it does not overflow.

quests.instruction: Why do cleaners usually work from top to bottom?
options: Tops are lighter to lift up ⚖️
Bottoms get cold sooner than tops 🧊
quests.hint: Gravity pulls dust down while you clean.
quests.explanation: Dust shaken off high shelves lands lower down. Cleaning the lower surfaces last picks it up.
quests.funFact: Cobwebs and ceiling dust are often cleaned first for this reason.

quests.instruction: A freshly mopped floor has dust falling onto it from a shelf. What went wrong?
quests.correctAnswer: The shelf should be dusted first 📚
options: The shelf should be dusted first 📚
The mop was far too clean 🪣
The floor was a bit too shiny ✨
quests.hint: What order would have stopped the dust from landing there?
quests.explanation: Dusting the shelves first means the falling dust lands before the floor is cleaned. Doing it afterward makes extra work.
quests.funFact: Doing dry jobs, like dusting, before wet jobs, like mopping, saves time.

quests.instruction: Which is the best order for cleaning a room?
quests.hint: Dry jobs come before wet jobs, and the floor comes last.
quests.explanation: Tidying clears the way, dusting drops dirt downward, sweeping gathers it, and mopping finishes the floor. The other orders undo earlier work.
quests.funFact: Many cleaning checklists follow exactly this order.

quests.instruction: Rina used the last of the paper towels and did not mention it. What is the responsible thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a grown-up it is out 🧻
options: Tell a grown-up it is out 🧻
quests.hint: Being responsible means helping others plan ahead.
quests.explanation: Telling an adult means a new roll can be bought before someone needs it. Hiding or returning an empty roll leaves the problem for the next person.
quests.funFact: A shopping list that everyone can write on keeps track of what is running low.

quests.instruction: Sam spilled paint on the rug and feels worried. What shows responsibility?
quests.hint: A fresh stain is easier to clean than an old one.
quests.explanation: Telling an adult quickly gives the best chance of cleaning the stain. Hiding it or blaming someone else makes things worse.
quests.funFact: Washable paint is easier to clean when it is still wet.

quests.instruction: A sibling forgot their turn to put the shoes away. What is a kind response?
quests.hint: A kind reminder helps both of you.
quests.explanation: A friendly reminder keeps things fair without an argument. Complaining causes fights, and always doing others' jobs is unfair to you.
quests.funFact: A turn chart on the wall shows everyone whose job is whose.

quests.instruction: A friend is arriving in ten minutes. How is the time best used?
quests.hint: Choose jobs that make the biggest difference quickly.
quests.explanation: In a short time, clearing floors and removing trash changes how the room looks and feels the most. Wardrobes and walls can wait.
quests.funFact: A ten-minute tidy can reset most rooms.

quests.instruction: A grown-up is mopping the kitchen floor. Where should a child stay?
options: Right in the middle of it 🚶
quests.hint: Water left behind makes a floor slippery.
quests.explanation: A freshly mopped floor is slippery, so wait for it to dry. Running or standing in the middle could cause a fall.
quests.funFact: Some people put out a yellow 'wet floor' sign while a floor dries.

quests.instruction: A room has scattered toys, a dusty shelf, a sticky floor spot, and a full trash can. What is the best order?
quests.correctAnswer: Trash, tidy toys, dust, then floor 🗑️
options: Floor, dust, then tidy toys, then trash 🧽
Trash, tidy toys, dust, then floor 🗑️
Dust, floor, then trash, then tidy toys 📚
quests.hint: Remove the biggest clutter first, and finish with the floor.
quests.explanation: Removing trash and tidying clears the way, dusting drops dirt downward, and the floor is last. The other orders would have you cleaning the floor twice.
quests.funFact: A checklist taped inside a cupboard can help children remember the order.
